title: An 'optional' header puts the presence dimension on the header name, not on the value inside it.
why: behavioural spec 'request': 'optional(of)' in a header map becomes an 'optional' whose 'of' is the 'each-like' the rule would otherwise have built, leaving the presence dimension on the header name itself (shape spec §6.4). The dimension id is the observable difference — 'request.headers.x-trace#presence' is a statement about whether the header is sent, which is what the author wrote, and no dimension at all is what the wrapped form produced by being rejected outright.
note: No exchange: a case's closure sends one fixed request on every variant, so it cannot both send and omit a header. What this case pins is the space the engine derived from the document the SDK built; 'live/forbidden-header-accepted' covers the round trip through the mock.

interaction.description: an order request whose trace header may be absent
